# --- The parameter lives here. This value is the DEFAULT. ---
# When you render from a script (or the command line) you can OVERRIDE it,
# e.g. quarto render canton-report.qmd -P canton:"Zürich"
params:
  canton: "Basel-Stadt"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# include: false means this chunk runs but produces no output in the report.
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# One shared dataset for the whole report.
cantons <- read_csv("swiss_cantons_dummy.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Everything below derives from params$canton + this dataset.
# Nothing about a specific canton is hard-coded.
this_canton <- params$canton

# Rank by population (1 = most populous), computed from the FULL table.
cantons <- cantons |>
  mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(population)))

# Pull out the single row for the selected canton.
row <- cantons |> filter(canton == this_canton)
```

## Overview

`r this_canton` is located in the **`r row$language_region`-speaking**
region of Switzerland.

As of the latest figures, `r this_canton` has a resident population of
**`r format(row$population, big.mark = "'", scientific = FALSE)`**, making it the
**`r row$rank``r ifelse(row$rank == 1, "st", ifelse(row$rank == 2, "nd", ifelse(row$rank == 3, "rd", "th")))`
most populous** of Switzerland's 26 cantons. Its area of
`r format(row$area_km2, big.mark = "'")` km² gives a population density of about
**`r round(row$population / row$area_km2)` people per km²**.

## This canton in national context

The table below places `r this_canton` alongside the national total and the
cantonal average. The **density** column is computed at render time
(population ÷ area) — it is not stored in the data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-context
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste(this_canton, "compared with national figures")
#| echo: false

national_total <- sum(cantons$population)
national_mean  <- mean(cantons$population)

context <- tibble(
  Measure    = c(this_canton, "National total", "Cantonal average"),
  Population = c(row$population, national_total, national_mean),
  `Area (km²)` = c(row$area_km2, sum(cantons$area_km2), mean(cantons$area_km2)),
  `Density (per km²)` = c(
    row$population / row$area_km2,
    national_total / sum(cantons$area_km2),
    national_mean  / mean(cantons$area_km2)
  )
)

context |>
  mutate(
    Population = round(Population),
    `Area (km²)` = round(`Area (km²)`),
    `Density (per km²)` = round(`Density (per km²)`)
  ) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = "'"))
```

## Where it sits among all cantons

@fig-pop shows every canton by population, with **`r this_canton` highlighted**.
The chart is drawn the same way every time — only the highlighted bar moves as
you change the parameter.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pop
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Resident population by canton.", this_canton, "is highlighted.")
#| fig-height: 6

cantons |>
  mutate(is_selected = canton == this_canton) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(canton, population), y = population, fill = is_selected)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#C8102E", `FALSE` = "grey70"),
                    guide = "none") +          # red = the Swiss flag colour
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = "'")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Resident population") +
  theme_minimal()
```
